target.title: fix(agents): log Anthropic provider rejections with status, redacted detail, and payload stats
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When Anthropic rejects a request ("LLM request failed: provider rejected the request schema or tool payload"), the error surfaces to the session/UI but nothing is written to gateway logs — operators cannot determine after the fact what status the provider returned, why it rejected the payload, or how large/tool-heavy the request was. Issue #103161 documents 6 such events in ~28 hours on a production gateway with zero corresponding log lines. This PR logs the rejection at the transport seam (real HTTP status, redacted provider detail, tool count, approximate payload size) plus a catch-all for non-HTTP transport failures, so these events become diagnosable from `gateway.log`.

## Summary

- Problem: When Anthropic rejects a request ("LLM request failed: provider rejected the request schema or tool payload"), the error reaches the session/UI but nothing lands in gateway logs — post-hoc diagnosis is impossible (#103161).
- Why it matters: Operators cannot see the HTTP status, the provider's error body, or the request shape (tool count / payload size) that triggered the rejection.
- What changed: `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.ts` gets a subsystem logger (`agent/anthropic-transport`). The non-ok response branch now logs a `warn` with the real `response.status`, the error-body snippet routed through `redactSensitiveText` + `truncateErrorDetail(..., 500)`, `toolCount`, and approximate payload size — mirroring the existing `[responses] error ...` convention in `openai-transport-stream.ts`. A second `warn` in the catch-all covers non-HTTP failures (aborts, malformed SSE) before `failTransportStream`.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): `transport-stream-shared.ts` (shared with OpenAI chat-completions and Google transports) is untouched — extending `failTransportStream` to log centrally for all three transports is noted as a possible follow-up seam; no logging-infrastructure or error-classification changes.

This is AI-assisted work (Claude conductor + Claude worker agents, human-operated); the diff was independently reviewed by a fresh-context model with an explicit secret-leak trace before submission.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #103161
- Related #
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: `anthropic-transport-stream.ts` had no subsystem logger at all. The non-ok branch read the error-body snippet and threw a bare `Error(detail)`; `response.status` and the body were known at that exact site but never logged. The catch-all called `failTransportStream` silently. The session-level `agent/embedded` warn log exists but regex-parses the HTTP code from the formatted message and carries no tool-count/payload-size.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no per-transport error logging for Anthropic (the OpenAI Responses transport has it; Anthropic and the chat-completions path do not).
- Contributing context (if known): `gateway.log`/`gateway.err.log` are the supervisor-captured console sink; `warn` passes the default console gate (`info`), so the new lines are visible by default without config changes.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: (1) a 400 `invalid_request_error` response produces a warn with `status: 400`, redacted detail, `toolCount`, and payload size — and a secret embedded in the provider error body (`sk-ant-api03-...`) never appears verbatim in ANY logged string; (2) a non-HTTP failure (malformed SSE frame on a 200) still produces the catch-all warn.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: unit tests at the exact transport seam, using the file's established mocked-fetch pattern and the repo's isolated `createSubsystemLogger` mock pattern (from `openai-transport-stream.test.ts`), with module state cleaned up in `finally`.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): none asserted logger calls in this file before.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A — two new tests added, written first and confirmed failing (0 warn calls) against unfixed code.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Provider rejections and Anthropic transport failures now produce `warn`-level `agent/anthropic-transport` lines in gateway logs (default-visible). No behavior change to requests, retries, error text shown to users, or failover classification.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
Anthropic 4xx -> throw Error(detail) -> session shows "LLM request failed: ..." -> logs: (nothing)

After:
Anthropic 4xx -> warn{status, redacted detail, toolCount, approxPayloadBytes} -> throw (unchanged)
non-HTTP failure -> warn "[messages] error provider=... model=... message=<redacted>" -> failTransportStream (unchanged)
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes`)
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: This change writes previously-unlogged provider error content to gateway logs. Mitigation: every content-bearing value is routed through `redactSensitiveText` (default `tools` mode: `sk-*` keys, Bearer tokens, registered secret values) BEFORE `truncateErrorDetail(..., 500)` (redact-then-truncate order so truncation cannot split a token past the patterns), on both log paths. This is load-bearing: the file-log sink passes structured meta to the logger unredacted, so the explicit pre-redaction is required, not belt-and-suspenders. A dedicated test asserts an embedded `sk-ant-api03-...` secret does not appear verbatim in either logged line. The request URL (which could carry query params) is not logged. Known pre-existing limitation (not introduced here): `redactSensitiveText` has no generic high-entropy catch-all, so a prefixless unregistered secret echoed by the provider would pass through — same exposure as every existing call site of the helper.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 26 (arm64); fix is platform-independent
- Runtime/container: Node 22 / bun, source checkout
- Model/provider: `anthropic/*` (any model routed through the Anthropic Messages transport)
- Integration/channel (if any): any (error is channel-independent)
- Relevant config (redacted): default logging config (file level info, console level info)

### Steps

1. Send a request the provider rejects (e.g. malformed tool schema → Anthropic HTTP 400 `invalid_request_error`).
2. Observe the session error "LLM request failed: provider rejected the request schema or tool payload."
3. Inspect gateway logs.

### Expected

- A `warn` `agent/anthropic-transport` line with status, redacted provider detail, tool count, and approximate payload size.

### Actual

- Before this PR: nothing in logs. After: expected line present (plus a catch-all summary line).

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Before (tests present, fix stashed): `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 2 times, but got 0 times` / `...called 1 times, but got 0 times`.

After:

```
pnpm test src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  104 passed (104)
```

Also green on the touched surface: scoped `tsgo:core` typecheck (exit 0), `oxfmt --check` clean. Note: repo-wide `pnpm check` fails in its preflight npm-shrinkwrap guard on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout in this environment — pre-existing and unrelated; this PR touches no lockfile/dependency files.

Reviewer notes (disclosed deliberately): (1) the catch-all logs user-initiated aborts at `warn`, which matches the existing OpenAI `[responses] error` behavior exactly — downgrading aborts to `debug` in both transports would be a reasonable follow-up; (2) an HTTP-rejection produces two warn lines (structured + catch-all summary) by design, asserted in tests; (3) `approxPayloadBytes` is `JSON.stringify(...).length` (UTF-16 code units), computed only on the error path — approximate by name and intent.

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: full test file locally (104/104) including the two new cases; redaction assertion with an embedded Anthropic-style key; the isolated-import mock pattern cleans up module state (doUnmock/resetModules in finally).
- Edge cases checked: non-HTTP failure path fires the catch-all independently (malformed SSE on HTTP 200); all four `createAnthropicMessagesClient` call sites (github-copilot, Foundry, OAuth, default) thread the new provider param; the function is internal (not exported), so no public surface change.
- What you did **not** verify: a live Anthropic 400 against the real API from a running gateway (validated at the transport seam with mocked fetch instead); log volume impact on high-cancel-rate deployments (matches existing OpenAI transport behavior).

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: sensitive content from provider error bodies reaching logs.
  - Mitigation: redact-then-truncate on every logged content field, tested with an embedded secret; no URL logging; same redaction helper and conventions as existing transports.
- Risk: increased warn-level log volume (two lines per rejection; aborts logged).
  - Mitigation: rejections are rare and exactly the events operators asked to see (#103161); abort logging matches the existing OpenAI transport convention.
